Date: 2025-12-11
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes (auto)
summary: Check-in on upcoming renewal (Mar 2026) and proposed capacity + EU private region pilot. Customer confirmed main concerns: latency at peak, data residency / KMS, and predictable monthly billing. Redwood affirmed path: reserved capacity uplift, eu-west private pilot, and security pack. Agreed next steps: SOW update, benchmark in eu-west-1, sample traffic, and decision call third week of Dec.
topics: pricing tiers and optional burst capacity
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta (Aurorae): Marta here. Daniel's on. Sameer and Rhea too.
[00:10] Jordan: Awesome. We booked 45, but looks like we have about 48. High level today: renewal planning, the region bump pilot in eu-west-1, and a quick perf/latency check. Priya, Luca with me.
[00:25] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, I'll jump into the benchmark plan in a bit.
[00:29] Daniel (Aurorae CTO): cool, we just pushed out a new model routing change last week so traffic shapes are different. hope that's OK for the bench.
[00:35] Sameer: yeah, we have those P95 spikes at 11am UTC — want to see behaviour there.
[00:40] Jordan: perfect, that's exactly what we'll emulate. Marta, quick ask — what's the exec ask on renewal? Are they looking to commit earlier, increase monthly units, or keep flat?
[00:52] Marta: Execs want predictability. Right now usage is variable — but they'd prefer a committed baseline we can depend on. Also EU data residency is non-negotiable for some of our customers.
[01:05] Rhea (Procurement): from procurement, we also need clarity on proration and how additional month-on-month top-ups work. Last time billing aligned but there were surprise line items.
[01:19] Jordan: noted. For proration we usually do a pro-rata charge for mid-cycle upsells; we'll put that in the SOW matrix. We'll also propose a two-tier reserved plan: baseline committed units + burst buffer for seasonal peaks.
[01:32] Priya: on the private region pilot — we propose eu-west-1 VPC with a private control plane (customer-managed VPC peering). That gives you KMS/HSM control, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM.
[01:45] Daniel: KMS is a must. We need to be able to use our AWS KMS keys, and audit trails have to match our retention policy.
[01:53] Priya: yes, we support customer-managed KMS; there might be a small ops lead time for the HSM certs but it's part of the onboarding checklist.
[02:02] Sameer: curious — do you guys support bring-your-own-HSM or is it limited? Past notes said HSM as an add-on.
[02:10] Priya: technically we support BYO-HSM for Private deployments; for Hosted there's a managed option. I'll attach the exact matrix in the security pack.
[02:18] Marta: what about latency — our internal SLA is 250ms median for inference. We saw 450ms P50 in last week's synthetic.
[02:28] Priya: okay, will test against 1k concurrent with your traffic profile to reproduce the 11am spikes. For eu-west-1 private we expect a median drop ~25-40% depending on model variant and kv cache hit rates.
[02:42] Daniel: when you say kv cache, are you referring to the prefix cache? sometimes the naming in the docs is different.
[02:49] Priya: sorry, yeah — KV cache meaning the key-value cache for the model context. docs sometimes say 'K V' cache or 'context cache' — transcription from other meetings has it split oddly.
[03:00] Jordan: ha, classic fireflies.
[03:03] Rhea: security-wise, SOC2 and ISO27001 copies please; also need a summary of encryption at rest + in transit.
[03:11] Jordan: will share SOC2 + ISO bundle and the short KMS/revocation note. Luca will also share the private deployment checklist.
[03:18] Luca (CSM): yep I'll put together a one-pager — networking, peering, firewall rules, expected lead times.
[03:25] Sameer: what about CA for egress IPs? We need predictable IP ranges for our allow lists.
[03:32] Priya: for dedicated/private we can provide static NAT egress IPs per cluster, and we'll include those in the runbook.
[03:39] Marta: great. On pricing, we need the committed unit price, burst pricing, and an optional discount if we commit to 12 months.
[03:47] Jordan: proposal: baseline commit 500k generation tokens/month, burst pool 200k, 12-month commit gets 10% off baseline unit price. We'll formalize in SOW.
[03:59] Daniel: can you show math for peak-day example? last month we had a day at 1.2M tokens.
[04:07] Priya: we'll include an example calc: baseline absorbs first 500k, burst covers 200k, remaining 500k billed at on-demand rates — we'll model three scenarios and include monthly spend ranges in the spreadsheet.
[04:21] Rhea: and what happens if we want to scale regionally before the renewal date? admin path?
[04:26] Jordan: we can do a mid-term amendment; typically we provision capacity and add to the next invoice cycle, pro-rated. There's also an option for fast-track provisioning for a one-time setup fee.
[04:36] Sameer: how long does the eu private pilot take from sign-off?
[04:40] Luca: from order form to green test cluster is typically 3-4 weeks if networking access and KMS are ready. If you need HSM provisioning it can add 1-2 weeks.
[04:50] Marta: timeline aligns with our compliance window in Feb. Good.
[04:54] Jordan: Priya, on the bench — can you outline the scope so Sameer can provide the traffic?
[05:00] Priya: plan is: 24 hour run in eu-west-1, supply two traffic loads (baseline and peak). We'll run 1k concurrent virtual clients and a 10% KV cache cold start pattern to simulate real user journeys. We'll measure P50/P95/P99, token cost, and error rate.
[05:17] Sameer: I'll export the 7-day sample and drop into the shared drive. We'll also flag any auth flows that might skew latencies.
[05:22] Daniel: question about graceful degradation — if capacity hits limit do you fallback to a cheaper model automatically? We want a predictable behavior.
[05:31] Priya: yes, Redwood has routing policies — can fallback to compatible lower-cost model variants. We can set a per-route policy: prefer baseline model, fallback to smaller quantized variant, and finally route to Hosted fallback in another region if private capacity is exhausted. We'll demo that in a follow-up technical deep-dive if you want.
[05:50] Marta: yes please. Also need to ensure data never leaves eu for certain records — can the fallback be restricted?
[05:57] Priya: fallback policies can be region restricted — you can configure a 'Sovereign' route. If no capacity exists within eu, the request fails rather than egressing. We'll document options.
[06:07] Rhea: procurement question: will the SOW include termination clauses for early reduction?
[06:12] Jordan: standard enterprise clause: early reduction requires 30-day notice and a small unwind fee for reserved capacity — we'll put exact terms in the amendment.
[06:20] Daniel: can we get a quick example of the billing sheet? last time it was a little dense.
[06:26] Jordan: yes, I'll attach an annotated workbook that shows baseline vs burst vs on-demand columns, with sample months.
[06:34] Priya: one more technical — will you want us to run the bench with and without quantization? Quantized models can drop cost but sometimes increase token latency.
[06:43] Marta: probably both — we need to see the quality tradeoffs.
[06:46] Priya: agreed. We'll schedule two runs: FP16-ish baseline and int8 quantized path. I'll note that quality tests will sit separately.
[06:55] Sameer: on the KMS integration, do you rotate keys via our KMS schedule or Redwood's? We prefer to keep rotation within our KMS.
[07:03] Priya: customer-managed KMS means rotation is yours; Redwood respects KMS policies and doesn't hold the plaintext keys. We'll include the key lifecycle diagram.
[07:12] Jordan: ok mid meeting check — everyone's aligned on baseline ask, private pilot in eu-west-1, and security docs. Any blockers?
[07:19] Marta: the only blocker is the finance sign-off on the 12-month discount; we need to present a clear cost projection to CFO.
[07:26] Rhea: timeline for that projection?
[07:29] Jordan: we'll aim to deliver the annotated cost workbook by 2025-12-15.
[07:34] Daniel: perfect.
[07:36] Priya: technical aside — for the benchmark we'll capture token-level cost and a small sample of logs. we'll obfuscate PHI if present, but Sameer, please flag any sensitive endpoints.
[07:47] Sameer: will do. We'll also provide a list of models you're currently hosting for us.
[07:52] Priya: we currently have three model families in your catalog: redwood-llama-lite-v2 (quant), redwood-chatgen-x, and a custom-tuned customer variant. names in transcripts sometimes get mangled.
[08:05] Jordan: okay, let's talk SLOs quickly — you're targeting median 250ms and P95 under 700ms. Can we commit to that for the pilot?
[08:14] Priya: we can commit to target SLOs for pilot but will put a note: SLO guarantees in contract are tied to committed throughput and prefix cache hit rates. We'll produce a table of expected SLO ranges per model + traffic profile.
[08:29] Marta: that caveat's fine as long as it's explicit.
[08:33] Jordan: last administrative — decision call? When should we reconvene?
[08:37] Marta: week of Dec 22 works, preferably Dec 23 morning for us.
[08:41] Jordan: will set tentative invite.
[08:43] Rhea: can you also send a redlined version of the amendment so legal can start loop?
[08:48] Jordan: yep, will include the amendment and a plain-language summary for legal.
[08:52] Luca: I'll also attach the private deployment runbook and an estimated provisioning timetable.
[08:58] Jordan: great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the SOW + bench plan.
[09:02] Marta: thanks all.
[09:05] [call ends]

Notes: transcript includes some imperfect ASR artifacts, product names occasionally transcribed inconsistently (e.g., 'K V cache', 'redwood-chatgen', 'sock two' for SOC2). References shared: security pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/scc/aurae-sec-pack), benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/aurorae-eu), SOW template (link: https://redwood.example.com/sow/template).
notes: Customer prioritized eu data residency and committed baseline. Team to produce SOW, run benchmark, and reconvene week of 2025-12-22.
